Any future dependency-review process must check the whole tree/offering, not just the root LICENSE file, before extracting even pattern-only knowledge - confirmed by LangGraph (langgraph-api Elastic 2.0) and Mastra (three tiers: framework/platform/enterprise) independently

Phase 4/7 CheckpointStore spec must treat retention/archival and schema-versioning/migration as first-class parts of the contract, not implementation details deferred to whichever backend is chosen - LangGraph's own open issues (#536 schema migration, #1138 unbounded growth) are direct evidence this is unsolved even in a mature, genuinely local-capable checkpointer

Mastra's Workspace is the strongest match found to LabLaunchPad's planned adapters/tools boundary combined with a policy layer - worth citing directly when Phase 8 (Capability Registry) and the tool-boundary Policy Gate design are formalized

Applies the same evidence-discipline rule used for the Youtu-Agent correction: re-check a finding against primary sources before treating it as settled, regardless of source (a user's steer is not exempt from this either - the correction itself was verified against LangGraph's own docs, not accepted on assertion alone)

decisions.contradiction: imported corpus CONTRADICTION-MATRIX.md #7 (LLM security judgement vs deterministic enforcement)
decisions.note: OpenHands' own docs state its LLM-based security analyzer is explicitly not a complete prompt-injection solution, and execute_tool() bypasses conversation analyzers/confirmation entirely - capability enforcement must live below the agent loop, not rely on model judgement. Directly actionable for this repository's own Policy Gate design. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Imported corpus's contradiction #3 (multi-agent coordination vs measurable coordination overhead) supports keeping single-agent as the default and multi-agent orchestration opt-in, not a default hierarchy. Consistent with this repository's own minimal-core bias; not yet cross-checked against the existing locked architecture per the corpus's own caveat that candidate deletions/changes need that comparison first.

The imported corpus proposes 6 ADR-CANDIDATEs (separate Runtime from Agent semantics; formalize State/Memory/Context/Knowledge/Evidence/Transcript; introduce ContextBroker; mandatory action-boundary policy for dangerous capabilities; opt-in multi-agent orchestration; semantic adapter policy for external frameworks) and 10 proposed benchmarks. None have been compared against the existing locked architecture (docs/architecture/PACKAGE-MAP.md, existing ADRs) or cross-checked against this session's own installment 1-3 findings yet - that reconciliation is future work, not performed as part of this import.
